column1: I. What is Democracy? Why Democracy?

column3: Democracy is a form of government where rulers are elected by the people.

column4: Final decision-making power must rest with those elected by the people.
Elections must offer a real choice and a fair chance for those in power to lose.

column3: One Person, One Vote, One Value

column4: Every adult citizen must have one vote, and each vote must carry equal value.
The government must rule within limits set by constitutional law and citizens' rights.

column3: It is a more accountable form of government, improves the quality of decision-making, provides a peaceful method to resolve conflicts, and enhances the dignity of citizens.
Modern democracy is typically a representative democracy because it is physically impossible for all citizens to sit together and take collective decisions.

It is the supreme law that determines the relationship among citizens and between the people and the government. It generates trust and coordination, specifies how the government is constituted, and limits governmental power.
After the struggle against apartheid (racial discrimination), South Africa created a constitution based on democratic values and human rights, ensuring no group was excluded.

column4: Prepared by the Constituent Assembly (299 members), which represented various social and political groups.
Adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into effect on 26 January 1950.
Contains the philosophy of the Constitution, emphasizing values like Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic, Justice, Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity.

column3: Elections are the mechanism by which people choose their representatives at regular intervals and change them if they wish.

column4: The country is divided into 543 Lok Sabha constituencies.
Seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes (84) and Scheduled Tribes (47) to ensure representation for weaker sections.
All citizens aged 18 and above have the right to vote under universal adult franchise.

column3: The EC is a very powerful, independent body in India that conducts and controls every aspect of elections.

column4: The final authority for making laws; consists of the President and two houses—Lok Sabha (House of the People) and Rajya Sabha (Council of States).
Includes the Prime Minister (head of government) and the Council of Ministers who take major policy decisions.
Civil servants who assist the political executive in day-to-day administration.
An independent and integrated system consisting of the Supreme Court, High Courts, and lower courts.

column3: The Supreme Court and High Courts have the power to determine the constitutional validity of any law or action of the executive.
Reasonable claims of persons recognized by society and sanctioned by law.

column4: Rule of law and prohibition of discrimination based on religion, race, caste, sex, or birth; includes the abolition of untouchability.
Includes freedom of speech and expression, assembly, association, and movement.
Prohibits human trafficking, forced labour (begar), and child labour.
India is a secular state where everyone can practice and propagate their chosen religion.
Allows minorities to conserve their culture and establish their own educational institutions.
Allows citizens to approach the Supreme Court or High Court to enforce their rights.
